commandGrammar.executionRule: Arguments are structured native argv, never a shell command string.

setupStateMachine.activationRule: An integration becomes active only after all selected assets and registrations are written transactionally and verification passes.
setupStateMachine.failureRule: Any failed stage restores its pre-operation snapshot and leaves unrelated configuration untouched.

must: identify only supported client candidates
discover the highest supported mechanism without treating generic project instructions as client identity
report available mechanisms and provisional fidelity without mutation
resolve all asset, config, symlink, junction, and reparse targets before mutation
show every proposed registration, path, backup, removal, fidelity, and release-binding change
show exact client configuration ownership boundaries
perform no write
require explicit user confirmation for a non-dry-run mutation
bind confirmation to the reviewed plan identity
reject changed or stale plans
prefer a supported native client install/update/remove API
otherwise use Agent Plugins package installation, then a supported native MCP/config registration, then only a required minimal bridge
copy versioned release-bound assets; never point an integration into the source checkout
preserve unrelated client configuration
stage backup and rollback data before activation
verify containment and asset integrity
verify skill discovery where claimed
start the client-owned MCP process where executable access is claimed
verify command resolution in the actual client launch environment
verify runtime identity, release version, required binding hashes, lifecycle behavior, and fidelity
fail closed before tools are exposed on a binding mismatch
read without mutation
report per-client selected mechanism, fidelity, health, bound release identity, missing surfaces, and exact remediation
distinguish disabled, removed, unavailable, damaged, and active
re-read current client state and produce a fresh preview
rebuild only Legion-owned damaged projections or registrations
refresh a release binding transactionally
never overwrite unrelated configuration
verify before reactivation
disable only Legion-owned activation or registration state
retain recoverable integration state and user configuration
not remove the machine-installed runtime
remove only the selected Legion integration and its verified owned assets
restore or remove only Legion-managed configuration entries
leave package-manager runtime uninstall independent
retain Legion state unless explicit purge is requested
require an explicit destructive confirmation
target only verified Legion-owned state roots
refuse ambiguous ownership, foreign paths, source checkout paths, and unresolved links
report exact removed roots and retained roots

transactionRules: No fallback configuration edit occurs before preview and confirmation.
Every fallback edit has a pre-operation backup and exact rollback route.
A client-specific failure cannot corrupt another client configuration.
Update cannot activate mixed runtime, asset, schema, catalog, or tool-contract versions.
Existing client processes may finish their bound release; incompatible state work waits for old leases to close.
No setup action starts an idle Legion daemon or a machine-wide socket.

sourceDiscrepancy.finding: The current Node descriptor engine performs projection and registration and is explicitly retired as a target semantic host shape.
sourceDiscrepancy.targetDisposition: replace with Rust-owned setup and mechanical per-client adapters; do not port its Legion semantic ownership.
